objectives: Identify shared rimes and changing onsets.
Build automaticity without guessing from pictures.
concepts: Words in a family share a rime.
Changing the onset can create another CVC word.
Controlled word lists keep decoding within taught patterns.

definitions.definition: The initial consonant sound before the vowel in a syllable.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.
A group of words that share the same rime.

workedExamples: bat, cat, sat share the -at rime.
commonMistakes: Changing the rime when only the onset should change.

conceptual: Identify shared rimes and changing onsets.
application: Decode a new taught-pattern word using its word family.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why changing one onset preserves the rime.
mixedReview: Mix b word families with previously taught CVC families.

quickRevision: find rime → say onset → blend → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If a word is misread, isolate the rime and rebuild the onset + rime blend.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the weakest b word family with fresh controlled words.

activities.name: Onset swap
steps: Check that the rime stayed the same.

outcomes: Learner decodes controlled b-pattern words using shared rimes.
Learner reads taught word-family chains accurately with increasing automaticity.

questions.question: A learner reads “bat” correctly but struggles with “cat.” What should be practised?
